equation_request.abstract: We introduce two multiple qubit controlled-unitary gates with different working principles. We employ these gates and existing quantum gates to propose simple and efficient algorithms that generate multi-term orthonormal entangled Bell-like bases. All algorithms thus far known for constructing entangled bases turn out to be special cases of our method. The Bell-like states in any basis is superposition of $2^{m}$-terms with equal probabilities (that is, their amplitudes being $\pm 1/\sqrt{2^{m}}$). The orthogonality of the basis does not permit arbitrary amplitudes. The quantum correlations of these bases are investigated; we find that the Bell-like bases obtained using different controlled-unitaries have different entanglement contents. We also learn that monogamy score is able to distinguish these bases in the situations where other quantum correlations fail to do so indicating that monogamy score is a more fundamental quantum correlation measure. Our approach can be extended to qudit systems as well.

specification.problem: Generate an orthonormal basis of n-qubit Bell-like states, each a uniform-magnitude superposition of 2^m terms with amplitudes +-1/sqrt(2^m), using Hadamards on m control qubits, a CNOT-fan controlled gate (type A) and CZ-style phase gates (type B), then check orthonormality and compute entanglement and monogamy measures classically from the statevector.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=3, m=1 (also n=4, m=2 as an optional extension). Qubit 0 is the control and qubits 1,2 are targets, with X gates on the inputs to set labels. Statevector only, no measurements. The paper's exact two controlled-unitary definitions, the proof that all earlier methods are special cases, the entanglement-measure computations and the qudit extension are outside scope except as noted.

symbols.meaning: injective GF(2)-linear map from controls to targets, given by the CNOT fan pattern
bit-flip label applied by X on the target inputs
phase label, set by the X-prepared control inputs before H
GF(2)-linear sign function for type B gates
Gram matrix of the basis statevectors

equations.label: Multi-term state
equations.description: Proposed form of the basis states: a type A fan-out of H-prepared controls, a phase label b on the controls and a bit-flip label a on the targets.
equations.justification: The abstract only states 2^m terms with amplitudes +-1/sqrt(2^m). This explicit form is my interpretation of the sketch.
assumptions: Gate order is H on controls, then CNOT fan, then labels as stated

equations.label: Amplitude magnitude
equations.description: Every nonzero amplitude has magnitude 1/sqrt(2^m) with sign +-1.

equations.label: Orthonormality
equations.description: The Gram matrix of all 2^n states should be the identity.
equations.abstract_quote: generate multi-term orthonormal entangled Bell-like bases
equations.justification: Orthonormality of the basis is claimed. For my eq_1 form, the overlap is nonzero only if f(c)+a = f(c)+a' for some c, i.e. a=a'. Then the sum over c of the characters gives delta_bb'. The count 2^m * 2^(n-m) = 2^n labels requires the a label to range over the full target space.

equations.label: Type B phase gate
equations.description: A CZ-style gate that attaches linear-character signs. Distinct w give different sign patterns.
equations.justification: This is my interpretation of a phase-type gate. The abstract does not define it.

equations.label: Monogamy score
equations.description: Classical postprocessing on the statevector. The one-vs-rest tangle is computed from the single-qubit purity, and the pairwise tangles are squared concurrences of reduced two-qubit states.
equations.justification: The standard residual-tangle form of monogamy score. The abstract's monogamy score may use another measure such as negativity.

registers.name: ctrl
registers.role: control qubits, H applied, hold the phase label b

registers.name: tgt
registers.role: target qubits, X-set to label a, fanned out by CNOTs

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |b>_ctrl |a>_tgt, set by X gates. In the actual circuit the b-bits are applied by X before the Hadamards, giving the phase character.

steps.description: Apply X on the control and target qubits according to the labels b and a.
Apply H on each control qubit.
Apply the type A CNOT fan: control i flips its prescribed subset of targets, realizing f(c).
Optionally apply type B CZ gates to attach extra signs (different bases).
Repeat for all labels, then compute the Gram matrix and check that the amplitudes are 0 or +-2^{-m/2}.
Compute reduced-state entropies and the monogamy score for each state.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Read the statevector of each label circuit. Build the Gram matrix and compare it with the identity. Check that nonzero amplitudes have magnitude 2^{-m/2}. Compute reduced density matrices, entropies, concurrence/tangle and monogamy score per state.
assumptions: Smallest instance n=3, m=1 chosen by me
The two gates are read as a bit-flip fan-out and a phase type
No black-box oracle appears, so no query budget applies
Qubit cap not stated; instances use at most 5 qubits
missing_information: Exact definitions of the paper's two multiple qubit controlled-unitary gates
Exact gate orderings for generating each basis
Which monogamy and correlation measures are used, and the numerical results
Why other bases are special cases
